Databento reaches $1.1 billion valuation in $100 million Series C
Nov 14, 2026, 9:45 PM UTC •
Tomáš Novák • 2 min read
Share this article
Save

Databento raised $100 million in a Series C round that values the market data platform at $1.1 billion. The company, which employs 39 people, counts five of the six largest frontier AI labs among its enterprise customers.
Databento, a market data platform serving the financial industry, raised $100 million in a Series C round that values the company at $1.1 billion.
Fifth Down Capital, which first backed Databento before it generated revenue, led the round. Most existing investors returned, including NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital and Hedosophia. Fitch Ventures joined as a strategic investor, bringing the perspective of a large financial information business with experience in credit ratings, financial data and market analysis.
The round closed months after a $97 million Series B. Since that earlier deal, Databento more than doubled its revenue and stayed profitable.
Databento's customers include quantitative trading firms, brokerages, asset managers, commodities businesses and digital asset firms. The company also holds enterprise agreements with five of the six largest frontier AI labs.
The company employed 39 people when the Series C closed. It reached the $1.1 billion valuation with a workforce smaller than those of conventional market data vendors.
"In this AI era, we're seeing remarkably small teams build billion-dollar companies, but that level of efficiency is unprecedented in the market data industry. Until now, reaching this milestone required hundreds of employees given the sheer scale of physical infrastructure involved. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished, and we'll continue to prioritize exceptional talent as we grow," Christina Qi, co-founder and CEO, said.
"Fifth Down first invested in Databento pre-revenue, as we recognized early on that the company had an opportunity to challenge the established model for delivering financial market data. Our confidence has only grown as Databento's traction and execution have demonstrated it can serve demanding institutional customers, sustain rapid growth, and build a profitable business. Databento's performance has reinforced our original thesis and strengthened our conviction in the company. We are thankful to Christina and Luca for the opportunity to increase our investment and involvement by leading the Series C financing," Andrew Spellman, founder and CEO of Fifth Down Capital, said.
Databento plans to spend the new capital on its market data infrastructure and on expanding coverage into more asset classes. The platform delivers live and historical data for futures, options, equities and indices through a single API. Because it controls each layer of its technology, from the original data source to final delivery, Databento says it is the first service of its kind to combine the speed and reliability that top trading firms require with a simpler experience for developers.
Source : Databento hits $1.1bn valuation with $100m Series C , by jhaxell , FinTech Global , Nov 13, 2026

Plural Raises USD 1.1 Billion to Invest in Europe's AI, Robotics and Defense Startups
Plural, a UK venture firm, raised EUR 1 billion (USD 1.10 billion) for its third fund. Two-thirds goes to early-stage startups, and the rest backs current portfolio companies. It targets energy, AI infrastructure, defense and healthcare. Six tech founders and executives lead the firm.
Written By:
Murali Teja
Reviewed By:
Manisha Sharma
Published on :
16 Nov 2026, 12:35 pm
Updated on :
16 Nov 2026, 12:35 pm
Copied
UK-based venture capital firm Plural has raised EUR 1 billion (USD 1.10 billion) for its third fund. The money will back technology startups across Europe. The firm plans to focus on energy, AI infrastructure, defense and healthcare.
The new fund shows that investors are paying more attention to European tech. Many of them want companies that build tools for key industries.
Pural Sets its Investment Priorities
Plural will put two-thirds of the fund into early-stage startups. The rest will go to companies it already backs. This extra money will help them grow.
The firm wants to find startups that can become large businesses. Its list of interests is wide. It includes AI infrastructure, chip making, the factories that produce chips, robotics and defense technology.
The firm does not plan to bet on just one area. It wants to back founders who know their field well and who want to build companies that compete around the world.
Six Partners Lead Plural's Investment Strategy
A group of tech founders and business leaders started Plural in 2022. Since then, it has invested in several European companies . These include Helsing, Proxima Fusion, OLIX and The Exploration Company.
Six partners lead the firm. They are Taavet Hinrikus, who co-founded Wise, and Sten Tamkivi, who co-founded Teleport. Ian Hogarth, who co-founded Songkick, is also a partner. So is Khaled Helioui, a former chief executive of Bigpoint. Carina Namih, who co-founded HelixNano, and Pierre-Dimitri Gore-Coty, a former Uber executive, complete the team.
Hinrikus said the firm has no fixed view on which sector will produce the next big company. Instead, the partners want to work with founders who have deep knowledge of their own industries.

A Boost for Europe's Strategic Technology Ambitions
The new fund adds fresh money to Europe's startup scene. Its focus on energy, chips, robotics and defense also fits a wider need. Europe wants stronger industry and more control over key technology.
For founders, the news means more support is available as they try to grow. For Plural, it means more room to back new ideas and to stand by the companies already in its portfolio.

articles.title: Estonia’s Plural raises €1bn to back Europe’s next technology giants
articles.snippet: Estonia’s Plural raises €1bn to back Europe’s next technology giants Estonian World
articles.text:
Estonia’s Plural raises €1bn to back Europe’s next technology giants
Plural’s team. The Tallinn- and London-based investment firm has raised €1 billion to back European technology companies in sectors including defence, energy, space and artificial intelligence. Photo: Plural.
By
Silver Tambur
· November 16, 2026 · Business · 4 minutes of reading
Share
Tweet
LinkedIn
Email
Plural, the investment firm co-founded by Estonian entrepreneurs Taavet Hinrikus and Sten Tamkivi, has raised €1 billion to back a generation of European technology companies seeking to compete on the world stage.
The firm, which operates from Tallinn and London, will invest in businesses tackling some of the continent’s most demanding technological challenges, from fusion energy and artificial intelligence infrastructure to defence and space.
The fundraising is the largest in Plural’s history and, according to figures cited by the Estonian business newspaper Äripäev, exceeds the amount raised by the entire Baltic private equity and venture capital industry last year.
It also carries a broader ambition: to help Europe build more of the companies on which its prosperity and security depend.
“For two decades, most of the world’s most valuable technology companies have been built in the US and China,” Plural said in its announcement. “Europe has been a customer rather than a creator, and that has cost us prosperity and bargaining power.”
A billion-euro commitment
The new capital is almost four times the €260 million Plural raised for its first fund in 2022 and double the €500 million raised for its second in 2024.
It will be divided roughly two to one. The larger share will finance new early-stage investments through Plural’s third fund; the remainder will go into a separate fund designed primarily to increase its stakes in leading companies already in its portfolio.
Plural’s proposition is to support founders from the outset and continue backing them as their companies grow.
“For too long, Europe has funded its best ideas in small instalments,” Carina Namih, a Plural partner, said in comments reported by Äripäev. “Founders raise a little, prove a little and then have to raise again. That is no way to build something complex.”
A field test by Estonian defence start-up Frankenburg Technologies, one of the companies backed by Plural, which has raised €1 billion in new capital. Photo: Frankenburg Technologies.
The firm’s portfolio includes Helsing in defence, Proxima Fusion in energy, The Exploration Company in space and Frankenburg Technologies, the defence company with roots in Tallinn. Plural-backed businesses have raised more than €3 billion in follow-on funding over the past year, according to the firm.
Growing ambitions
For Estonia, the fundraising offers evidence that its technology industry is developing beyond the generation of companies that established its international reputation.
Hinrikus co-founded Wise and was Skype’s first employee. Tamkivi was an early Skype executive and later co-founded Teleport. Their investment firm now backs founders attempting to build businesses in fields far removed from money transfers and internet calls.
“Several of the founders behind that success are building companies again, this time tackling much tougher challenges. Global ones,” Tamkivi told Äripäev. “Frankenburg is a good example of how a company founded in Tallinn can become an international player in the defence industry.”

articles.snippet: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, we're announcing that we've raised $1B in a Series A, led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with participation from Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google, M13, Pear VC, and S32, among other new and existing investors....
articles.text:
Mirendil Raises $1B to Democratize Frontier AI R&D
News provided by
Mirendil
Nov 12, 2026, 12:30 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, we're announcing that we've raised $1B in a Series A, led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with participation from Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google, M13, Pear VC, and S32, among other new and existing investors.
We believe making AI R&D more accessible is the most direct path to AI that solves humanity's most pressing problems across science and technology. We're building tools to democratize frontier AI R&D and help put it within reach of every scientist and engineer.
Over the past three weeks, we've shared our first results, and they point to the same shift: when agents do the hands-on work, the size of your team stops limiting what you can build. One researcher, working with agents, pretrained Mirendil-Base , a competitive coding model, from scratch in 3.5 months with less than $10M in compute. We then post-trained it into Fern , which holds up to 10M tokens of context, enough for days of an agent's work. And Lor , now in private beta, brings this way of working to everyone else: hundreds of agents writing code and running experiments for days at a time. Mirendil runs on Lor every day.
This round lets us go further, toward a world where one person can take on what used to need a team, a team what used to need an institution, and we can help accelerate science and technology in a more direct way than we've done before.
We're still a small team with a singular focus. If you want to help make frontier AI R&D accessible to everyone, join us . If you'd like to build with Mirendil, we'd like to hear from you at [email protected] .

Key points
Mirendil raised a $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google, M13, Pear VC and S32 also investing; it did not disclose a valuation [1] .
The round follows a $200 million seed in June at a $1 billion valuation, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins with Nvidia joining [5] ; reports in September said Mirendil was seeking up to $1 billion at a $5 billion valuation [6] .
Mirendil says one researcher working with agents pretrained its Mirendil-Base coding model from scratch in 3.5 months for less than $10 million in all-in compute, with agents writing more than 99% of the code [2] .
Its products are Fern, a model with a context window of up to 10 million tokens, and Lor, a private-beta platform that runs hundreds of agents writing code and running experiments for days [1] [3] [4] .
Mirendil, a startup founded by two former Anthropic researchers to automate the work of building AI, has raised $1 billion in a Series A round led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, the company said on Thursday, Nov. 12 [1] . Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google , M13, Pear VC and S32 also invested, along with other new and existing investors. Mirendil did not disclose its valuation [1] .
The round comes five months after a $200 million seed at a $1 billion valuation, which Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins co-led and Nvidia joined [5] . In September, reports said the company was in talks to raise up to $1 billion at a $5 billion valuation with Kleiner Perkins leading [6] ; Mirendil's announcement confirms the size and the lead but not the price.
One researcher, 3.5 months, under $10 million
Mirendil's pitch is that agents can now do most of the hands-on work of an AI lab, so a small team can build what used to take an institution. "When agents do the hands-on work, the size of your team stops limiting what you can build," the company wrote [1] .
Its main evidence is Mirendil-Base, a coding model it published results for on Oct. 21. Mirendil says a single researcher, working with agents, pretrained it from scratch in 3.5 months with less than $10 million in compute, a figure it describes as all-in, including the agents' token spend, data processing and every small-scale experiment [2] . Agents wrote more than 99% of the code, ran experiments and diagnosed failures, while the researcher decided what to try and what to trust; the company says it used only publicly available data, no distillation and no licensed datasets [2] . These are Mirendil's own figures and have not been independently replicated.
Mirendil then post-trained the base model into Fern, which it says can hold up to 10 million tokens in context, about half a million lines of code or days of an agent's work at once [3] . Fern 0.1 is listed at 0.1 to 0.5 trillion parameters, with access "coming soon"; larger Mirendil-Base-Large and Mirendil-Base-XL models, at up to 2 trillion and 10 trillion parameters, are still in pretraining [3] . articles.text:
CKX Lands: $1 Billion Brad Jacobs Investment To Launch New Public Company Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:15 AM
CKX Lands: $1 Billion Brad Jacobs Investment To Launch New Public Company Platform
Jacobs Private Equity II and minority co-investors have agreed to invest $1 billion in CKX Lands, creating a public company platform that Brad Jacobs plans to use to build a business in an industry that has not yet been selected.
Jacobs Private Equity will provide $900 million, while co-investors led by HRTG Partners will contribute $100 million. Jacobs Private Equity will hold a majority interest following the transaction.
Brad Jacobs will become chairman and chief executive officer of CKX while continuing to serve in the same roles at building products distributor QXO.
CKX will be renamed and operate as a separate public company. Before closing, it will convert from a Louisiana corporation to a Delaware corporation, complete a holding-company reorganization, and conduct a 4.1744380-for-1 reverse stock split.
The investors will receive voting convertible perpetual preferred shares convertible into approximately 219 million common shares at $4.57 per post-split share. They will also receive warrants to purchase approximately 219 million additional shares at exercise prices ranging from $4.57 to $13.70.
Following closing and before warrant exercises, Jacobs Private Equity and its co-investors will own approximately 99.78% of the company on a fully convertible and exchangeable basis.
CKX will declare a $20.8 million cash dividend, equal to $10.1312 per existing share, before the transaction closes. Existing investors will retain exposure to CKX’s land business while participating in the potential future company.
The board unanimously approved the investment, and shareholders representing approximately 28% of voting power agreed to support it. Completion is expected in early 2027, subject to shareholder approval and other conditions.
Jacobs has founded or led eight billion-dollar or multibillion-dollar companies and participated in approximately 500 acquisitions. The new platform would become his ninth company.
KEY QUOTES
“I love building multibillion-dollar market leaders, and this $1 billion investment marks the launch of my ninth company. After concluding my chairmanships of XPO, GXO, and RXO last year, I now have the capacity to create this new venture while continuing to lead QXO to its massive potential.”
Brad Jacobs, Founder of Jacobs Private Equity II
“We believe this investment will create compelling outcomes for our stakeholders, including the opportunity for our stockholders to receive a substantial upfront cash payment as part of a $20.8 million dividend. We expect our stockholders will benefit from retaining the value of our existing land business while also participating in the potential upside of Brad Jacobs’ future plans for the company.”
William Gray Stream, President of CKX Lands

This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here .
It was another big week for AI-related startup financings. Mirendil , a developer of agentic AI for R&D, led the pack with a $1 billion series A, followed by Mercor , which secured $750 million to connect AI developers with human experts.
Overall, the vast majority of this week’s largest rounds were AI-related, though we did see some biotech, fintech and enterprise software in the mix.
1. Mirendil , $1B, AI for R&D: Mirendil, a developer of agentic AI technology for research and development, secured $1 billion in a Series A funding. Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital led the round for the San Francisco-based startup.
2. Mercor , $750M, human-led AI training: Mercor, a platform that connects AI developers with human experts for model training and evaluation, raised $750 million in Series D funding. The round, backed by a long list of venture investors, set a $20 billion valuation for the San Francisco-based company, which was founded less than four years ago.
3. Torus , $500M, AI infrastructure: Salt Lake City-based Torus, a manufacturer of distributed power and compute infrastructure, announced a $500 million growth financing led by Magnetar Capital . It also introduced a product called Foundry, described as modular AI infrastructure for inference compute.
4. (tied) Path Robotics , $300M, AI for manufacturing: Path Robotics, a developer of physical AI technology for robotics and manufacturing, with initial expertise in welding, picked up $300 million in Series E financing. Georgian led the round, which set a $2.45 billion valuation for the Columbus, Ohio-based company.
4. (tied) LangChain , $300M, agentic AI: LangChain, developer of a platform to run, improve and govern AI agents, closed on $300 million in Series C funding at a $3 billion valuation. CapitalG led the round for the 4-year-old, San Francisco-based company.
6. Nominal , $240M, hardware engineering tools: Nominal, a developer of intelligence tools for hardware engineering, raised $240 million at a $3 billion valuation. Lightspeed Venture Partners and Insight Partners led the round for the Austin-based startup.
7. (tied) Imprint , $130M, fintech: Imprint, a payments, loyalty and customer intelligence platform for brands, landed $130 million in new funding at a $1.9 billion valuation. Khosla Ventures led the financing for the 6-year-old, New York-based company.
7. Corma, an Israeli-founded cybersecurity startup that builds AI models and agents for defense, has raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation, Ynetnews reported . Company Corma, Israeli-founded, AI models and agents for cyber defense
Round $125 million Series A
Valuation $1 billion
Lead investor NEA
